title: Judge props and supports at player scale and in their actual operating states
trigger: bookcase shelving book scale avatar cabinet frame flush hinge interaction support beam pillar brace clutter
guidance: Use the established avatar as a scale reference and size ordinary props plausibly around it. The owner's five-to-six book rows per person is a visual calibration reference, not a mandatory shelf count. Do not shrink the actor to accommodate oversized furnishings or inadequate circulation. Inspect actual closed/open mesh bounds, bind pivots, back planes and operating sweeps together with the real player collider. When a control promises cabinet opening, exercise that control in the dungeon; a workshop hinge pose is only a partial check. Distinguish local decorative state from game-owned storage/inventory. Add supports at meaningful corners, joins and long spans according to room size/use, with independent optional strategies and stair-clearance checks, rather than filling every available location.

evidence.reference: codex-thread:01a16a2c-da7b-7042-9108-3dbbc26da0f6; owner bookshelf/avatar comparison and five-item cabinet/timber/stair QC
evidence.note: Owner says the avatar is the correct scale, books appear as large as an arm, cabinet doors must fit/open, and support placement should avoid pointless clutter.

Recorded correction measures the cabinet gap, preserves source UVs, guards sweeps and uses the actual movement radius for optional post admission. Recheck current bounds; the old offset is not a repair constant.

recheck: Review the current avatar, imported mesh/frame conversion, player radius, furniture operating bounds and room purpose. Painted skin accessories are not automatically geometry, and visible storage bays are not inventory authority.
